summary: Public entry-point functions for retrieving cached settings instances. get_settings() is the primary interface — it normalises inputs into a SettingsParameters, retrieves or creates a cached instance via _get_settings() (LRU-cached), then applies runtime overrides. get_settings_manager() returns the SettingsManager singleton.
lifecycle_notes: _get_settings() is @lru_cache(maxsize=None) — unbounded cache keyed on SettingsParameters structural hash
get_settings_manager() is also @lru_cache — returns a process-wide singleton SettingsManager
Runtime kwargs are applied after cache retrieval via apply_runtime_overrides(), never polluting the cached instance
documentation_hooks: Two-level caching: lru_cache on _get_settings() for structural identity; SettingsManager dict as secondary store
get_settings() accepts either a pre-built SettingsParameters or individual keyword arguments
risks: lru_cache is process-global and never cleared — in long-running processes, settings changes (e.g. env var mutation) will not be picked up after first load
